subject: Storage zones that improve kitchen flow
hook: Most kitchens are not short of cupboards. They are short of the right things in the right place.
ig:
Most kitchens are not short of cupboards. They are short of the right things in the right place.

Planning a kitchen in storage zones is the simplest way to fix that. Think about the order you actually work in:

1. Food storage: larder, fridge and dry goods together.
2. Crockery and cutlery: within one step of the dishwasher.
3. Cleaning: sink, bin and products as one unit of space.
4. Preparation: the longest clear worktop, ideally between sink and hob, with knives and boards in the drawers below.
5. Cooking: pans, oils and utensils right next to the hob.

Get the order right and you stop crossing the room with a dripping colander or a stack of plates. It is the foundation of every bespoke kitchen layout we plan, whatever the size of the room.

Save this before you start looking at door colours. Layout first, finishes second. When you are ready, the link in bio takes you to our kitchens page.
fb:
Here is a simple test for your kitchen: how many steps does it take to unload the dishwasher? If the answer involves walking to the other side of the room, your storage is working against you.

When we plan a bespoke kitchen, we start with five zones: food, crockery, cleaning, prep and cooking, laid out in the order you work. Pans by the hob, plates by the dishwasher, bin by the sink. It sounds obvious, but most kitchens grow without a plan and end up muddled.
